faults.fault: Disable exactly one Azure VXC/MSEE path without changing overlay configuration.
faults.restore: Re-enable the same VXC and wait for provider and BGP state to return.
faults.pass: The ER service remains usable through the surviving MSEE path and probes have no sustained failure.

faults.fault: Disable both Azure VXCs or the vHub ER connection using the reviewed reversible operation.
faults.restore: Restore both paths and prove serviceProviderProvisioningState=Provisioned before proceeding.
faults.pass: D2 moves to the Internet overlay; D3 uses the Internet aggregate when healthy; D1 behavior is classified at the exact failed layer.

faults.fault: Stop or administratively disable only the selected StrongSwan child/IKE association.
faults.restore: Reload and initiate only the affected connection; do not alter BGP policy.
faults.pass: Only routes dependent on that IPsec path withdraw and the surviving design path carries probes.

faults.fault: Administratively shut only the selected FRR neighbor while leaving IKE/IPsec established.
faults.restore: No-shut the same neighbor and wait for the original route set.
faults.pass: Captures prove SAs stay up while BGP routes withdraw; forwarding follows the remaining eligible route.

faults.fault: Apply the reviewed narrow drop to the application flow while underlay, IKE/IPsec and BGP stay healthy.
faults.restore: Remove the exact drop rule and verify counters stop increasing.
faults.pass: The harness distinguishes application/data-plane loss from control-plane health; no false route failover is claimed.

faults.fault: Remove or block only the CPE public underlay reachability using the reviewed reversible operation.
faults.restore: Restore public reachability and both public active-active tunnel slots.
faults.pass: The private ER overlay remains healthy; only Internet-dependent routes and probes change.

faults.fault: First fail the Internet backup, prove the static aggregate remains installed, then withdraw the ER/BGP more-specifics.
faults.restore: Restore ER more-specifics first, then Internet, then run the full reset gate.
faults.pass: The expected blackhole is proved by route presence plus packet/probe loss, or health automation withdraws the aggregate and that behavior is captured.
